topics.title: Location, size and boundaries (अवस्थिति, आकार र सिमाना)

questions.label: Expected – Practice
questions.stem: What is the present official area of Nepal?
questions.explanation: The map of 2077 BS added 335 sq km (Limpiyadhura, Lipulekh, Kalapani) to the earlier 147,181 sq km.

questions.label: Expected – Practice
questions.stem: Nepal Standard Time is based on the meridian that passes through:
questions.explanation: The meridian 86°15′ E passes through Gaurishankar Himal in Dolakha. Nepal's time is 5 hours 45 minutes ahead of Coordinated Universal Time.

questions.label: Pattern-Based – Reconstructed
questions.stem:
Read the statements.

  1. Nepal touches five states of India.
  2. Karnali Province has no boundary with India.
  3. Madhesh Province has a boundary with China.
  4. Taplejung and Darchula touch both India and China.

Which statements are correct?
questions.explanation: Statement 3 is wrong. Madhesh touches only India. Lumbini also has no boundary with China.

questions.label: Pattern-Based – Reconstructed
questions.stem:
Match List I with List II.

List I List II
A. Southern limit 1. 88°12′ E
B. Northern limit 2. 26°22′ N
C. Western limit 3. 80°04′ E
D. Eastern limit 4. 30°27′ N
questions.explanation: Latitudes (N) give the south and north limits; longitudes (E) give the west and east limits. The smaller number is always the south or the west.

questions.label: Expected – Practice
questions.stem: The eastern and western ends of Nepal are about 8° of longitude apart. Because the earth turns 1° in 4 minutes, the difference in local sun time between the two ends is about:
questions.explanation: 8° × 4 minutes = 32 minutes. The whole country still uses one standard time.

topics.title: Physiographic regions (भौगोलिक प्रदेश)

questions.label: Expected – Practice
questions.stem: In the traditional three-fold division, what share of Nepal's area is hill (Pahad)?
questions.explanation: Himal 15%, Pahad 68%, Terai 17%.

questions.label: Pattern-Based – Reconstructed
questions.stem:
Arrange from south to north.

  1. Mahabharat range
  2. Chure hills
  3. Terai
  4. Great Himalaya
questions.explanation: The Terai is the southernmost belt. The Chure rises next, then the higher Mahabharat, and last the Great Himalaya.

questions.label: Pattern-Based – Reconstructed
questions.stem: Which one does not belong to the group?
questions.explanation: Chitwan, Dang and Surkhet are Inner Terai (Dun) valleys between the Chure and the Mahabharat. Pokhara is a midland valley.

questions.label: Pattern-Based – Reconstructed
questions.stem:
Assertion (A): The Terai holds more than half of Nepal's population.

Reason (R): The Terai covers more than half of Nepal's area.
options: Both A and R are true, and R explains A.
Both A and R are true, but R does not explain A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.
questions.explanation: In the Census of 2078 the Terai had 53.61% of the people, but it covers only about 17% of the land.

questions.label: Expected – Practice
questions.stem: Which fault separates the Chure hills from the Terai plain?
questions.explanation: From north to south the order is Central, Boundary, Frontal. The Main Frontal Thrust is the southernmost and runs along the foot of the Chure.

topics.title: Mountains, passes and glaciers (हिमाल, भन्ज्याङ र हिमनदी)

questions.label: Expected – Practice
questions.stem: How many of the world's fourteen peaks above 8,000 m are in Nepal?
questions.explanation: Sagarmatha, Kanchenjunga, Lhotse, Makalu, Cho Oyu, Dhaulagiri, Manaslu and Annapurna.

questions.label: Pattern-Based – Reconstructed
questions.stem:
Arrange the peaks from east to west.

  1. Dhaulagiri
  2. Makalu
  3. Manaslu
  4. Kanchenjunga
questions.explanation: Kanchenjunga (Taplejung) is the easternmost. Then come Makalu (Sankhuwasabha), Manaslu (Gorkha) and Dhaulagiri (Myagdi).

questions.label: Pattern-Based – Reconstructed
questions.stem:
Match the pass with its district.

Pass District
A. Korala 1. Rasuwa
B. Kodari 2. Mustang
C. Rasuwagadhi 3. Darchula
D. Tinkar 4. Sindhupalchok
questions.explanation: Korala is in Mustang, Kodari in Sindhupalchok, Rasuwagadhi in Rasuwa and Tinkar in Darchula.

questions.label: Expected – Practice
questions.stem: Which is the highest peak that lies wholly inside Nepal?
questions.explanation: Kanchenjunga stands on the border with India; Makalu and Cho Oyu stand on the border with China. Dhaulagiri I (8,167 m) is wholly in Nepal.

questions.label: Pattern-Based – Reconstructed
questions.stem:
Read the statements.

  1. Annapurna I was the first peak above 8,000 m to be climbed.
  2. The height of 8,848.86 m for Sagarmatha was announced in 2020.
  3. Cho Oyu lies in Taplejung district.

Which statements are correct?
questions.explanation: Cho Oyu lies in Solukhumbu. Kanchenjunga is the eight-thousander of Taplejung.

topics.title: Rivers and lakes (नदी र ताल)

questions.label: Expected – Practice
questions.stem: Which is the longest river of Nepal?
questions.explanation: The Karnali flows for 507 km inside Nepal. The Koshi is the largest river, not the longest.

questions.label: Pattern-Based – Reconstructed
questions.stem: Which one does not belong to the group?
questions.explanation: Tamor, Likhu and Indrawati are branches of the Koshi. The Marsyangdi is a branch of the Gandaki.

questions.label: Pattern-Based – Reconstructed
questions.stem:
Match the river with its name in India.

River in Nepal Name in India
A. Karnali 1. Sharda
B. Narayani 2. Ghaghara
C. Mahakali 3. Gandak
questions.explanation: Karnali becomes the Ghaghara, Narayani becomes the Gandak, and Mahakali becomes the Sharda.

questions.label: Expected – Practice
questions.stem: The Kali Gandaki and the Trishuli meet to form the Narayani at:
questions.explanation: Devghat lies where Chitwan, Tanahun and Nawalpur meet. Chatara is on the Koshi and Chisapani is on the Karnali.

questions.label: Pattern-Based – Reconstructed
questions.stem:
Read the statements.

  1. Rara is the largest lake of Nepal and lies in Mugu.
  2. Tilicho lies in Manang.
  3. Phoksundo lies in Jumla.
  4. Phewa lies in Kaski.

Which statements are correct?
questions.explanation: Phoksundo lies in Dolpa, not Jumla.

topics.title: Climate, soil, natural vegetation and forest (हावापानी, माटो, वनस्पति र वन)

questions.label: Expected – Practice
questions.stem: Which date does the Department of Hydrology and Meteorology use as the normal date of monsoon onset in Nepal?
questions.explanation: The normal onset is 13 June and the normal withdrawal is 2 October.

questions.label: Pattern-Based – Reconstructed
questions.stem:
Assertion (A): Mustang and Manang receive very little rain.

Reason (R): They lie in the rain shadow north of the Annapurna and Dhaulagiri ranges.
options: Both A and R are true, and R explains A.
Both A and R are true, but R does not explain A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.
questions.explanation: The monsoon wind drops its rain on the southern slopes. Little moisture is left when the air crosses to the northern side.

questions.label: Pattern-Based – Reconstructed
questions.stem:
Match the soil with the area where it is mainly found.

Soil Area
A. Alluvial 1. Kathmandu Valley
B. Lacustrine 2. Himalayan belt
C. Sandy and gravelly 3. Terai
D. Glacial 4. Chure and Bhawar
questions.explanation: Alluvial soil is found in the Terai, lacustrine soil in the Kathmandu Valley, sandy and gravelly soil in the Chure and Bhawar, and glacial soil in the Himalayan belt.

questions.label: Expected – Practice
questions.stem: Sal forest is typical of which belt?
questions.explanation: Sal grows in the hot Terai, Inner Terai and Chure, below about 1,200 m.

questions.label: Pattern-Based – Reconstructed
questions.stem: Fill in the blank. According to the land-cover figures published by the Forest Research and Training Centre in 2024, forest and other wooded land together cover about ______ of Nepal.
questions.explanation: Forest 43.38% and other wooded land 2.70% make 46.08%. The figure 44.74% is the 2015 total.

topics.title: Protected areas and biodiversity (संरक्षित क्षेत्र र जैविक विविधता)

questions.label: Expected – Practice
questions.stem: Which is the largest national park of Nepal?
questions.explanation: Shey Phoksundo covers 3,555 sq km in Dolpa and Mugu. The Annapurna Conservation Area is larger, but it is not a national park.

questions.label: Pattern-Based – Reconstructed
questions.stem: Three of the following are on the World Heritage List. Which one is not?
questions.explanation: Nepal's World Heritage Sites are Sagarmatha National Park, Chitwan National Park, the Kathmandu Valley and Lumbini.

questions.label: Pattern-Based – Reconstructed
questions.stem:
Match the protected area with the animal it is best known for.

Protected area Animal
A. Koshi Tappu 1. Blue sheep
B. Shuklaphanta 2. One-horned rhinoceros
C. Dhorpatan 3. Wild water buffalo
D. Chitwan 4. Swamp deer
questions.explanation: Koshi Tappu protects the wild water buffalo, Shuklaphanta the swamp deer, Dhorpatan the blue sheep and Chitwan the one-horned rhinoceros.

questions.label: Pattern-Based – Reconstructed
questions.stem:
Read the statements.

  1. Nepal has 12 national parks.
  2. Nepal has 3 wildlife reserves.
  3. Nepal has 10 Ramsar sites.
  4. Nepal has 6 conservation areas.

Which statements are correct?
questions.explanation: Nepal has one wildlife reserve, Koshi Tappu. Shuklaphanta and Parsa became national parks in 2017.

questions.label: Expected – Practice
questions.stem: Which was the first wetland of Nepal to be listed as a Ramsar site?
questions.explanation: Koshi Tappu was listed in 1987. Three more sites followed in 2003.

topics.title: Administrative geography and superlatives (प्रशासनिक भूगोल र विशेषता)

questions.label: Expected – Practice
questions.stem: How many rural municipalities (गाउँपालिका) are there in Nepal?
questions.explanation: The 753 local levels are 6 metropolitan cities, 11 sub-metropolitan cities, 276 municipalities and 460 rural municipalities.

questions.label: Pattern-Based – Reconstructed
questions.stem:
Arrange the provinces by area, largest first.

  1. Koshi
  2. Karnali
  3. Madhesh
  4. Bagmati
questions.explanation: Karnali 27,984 sq km, Koshi 25,905 sq km, Bagmati 20,300 sq km, Madhesh 9,661 sq km.

questions.label: Pattern-Based – Reconstructed
questions.stem:
Match the province with its capital.

Province Capital
A. Lumbini 1. Godawari
B. Sudurpashchim 2. Hetauda
C. Bagmati 3. Deukhuri
D. Karnali 4. Birendranagar
questions.explanation: Lumbini–Deukhuri, Sudurpashchim–Godawari, Bagmati–Hetauda, Karnali–Birendranagar.

questions.label: Pattern-Based – Reconstructed
questions.stem:
Read the statements.

  1. Bagmati Province has the largest population.
  2. Madhesh Province has the highest population density.
  3. Koshi Province has the largest number of districts.
  4. Karnali Province has the largest number of local levels.

Which statements are correct?
questions.explanation: Karnali has the fewest local levels (79). Koshi has the most (137).

questions.label: Expected – Practice
questions.stem: Which two former districts were each divided between two provinces?
questions.explanation: Nawalparasi was divided between Gandaki and Lumbini, and Rukum between Lumbini and Karnali. This raised the number of districts from 75 to 77.

topics.title: Hydropower and natural resources (जलविद्युत् र प्राकृतिक स्रोत)

questions.label: Expected – Practice
questions.stem: Which was the first hydropower station of Nepal?
questions.explanation: Pharping (500 kW) opened in 1911 (1968 BS).

questions.label: Pattern-Based – Reconstructed
questions.stem:
Arrange by capacity, largest first.

  1. Kali Gandaki A
  2. Upper Tamakoshi
  3. Kulekhani I
  4. Arun III
questions.explanation: Arun III 900 MW, Upper Tamakoshi 456 MW, Kali Gandaki A 144 MW, Kulekhani I 60 MW. Arun III is still under construction.

questions.label: Pattern-Based – Reconstructed
questions.stem:
Match the project with its district.

Project District
A. Kulekhani 1. Sankhuwasabha
B. Kali Gandaki A 2. Makawanpur
C. Upper Tamakoshi 3. Syangja
D. Arun III 4. Dolakha
questions.explanation: Kulekhani is in Makawanpur, Kali Gandaki A in Syangja, Upper Tamakoshi in Dolakha and Arun III in Sankhuwasabha.

questions.label: Expected – Practice
questions.stem: Which river basin has the largest theoretical hydropower potential?
questions.explanation: Karnali and Mahakali 36,180 MW; Koshi 22,350 MW; Gandaki 20,650 MW; southern rivers 4,110 MW.

questions.label: Pattern-Based – Reconstructed
questions.stem:
Read the statements.

  1. Nepal first sent electricity to Bangladesh through India's grid in November 2024.
  2. The Sunkoshi–Marin Diversion is designed to irrigate land in Madhesh Province.
  3. Kharidhunga in Dolakha is known for magnesite.

Which statements are correct?
questions.explanation: All three are correct. The first flow to Bangladesh, 40 MW, took place on 15 November 2024.

topics.title: Map-based General Knowledge (नक्सामा आधारित सामान्य ज्ञान)

questions.label: Pattern-Based – Reconstructed
questions.stem:
Arrange the provincial capitals from east to west.

  1. Pokhara
  2. Janakpurdham
  3. Birendranagar
  4. Biratnagar
questions.explanation: Biratnagar (Koshi), Janakpurdham (Madhesh), Pokhara (Gandaki), Birendranagar (Karnali).

questions.label: Pattern-Based – Reconstructed
questions.stem:
Match the district with its headquarters.

District Headquarters
A. Khotang 1. Gulariya
B. Bardiya 2. Manma
C. Kalikot 3. Malangwa
D. Sarlahi 4. Diktel
questions.explanation: Khotang–Diktel, Bardiya–Gulariya, Kalikot–Manma, Sarlahi–Malangwa.

questions.label: Pattern-Based – Reconstructed
questions.stem: A traveller goes from east to west along the Mahendra Highway. In which order are these rivers crossed?
questions.explanation: The Koshi is in the east, the Bagmati in Madhesh, the Narayani at the edge of Chitwan and the Karnali in the far west.

questions.label: Pattern-Based – Reconstructed
questions.stem: Which one does not belong to the group?
questions.explanation: Mustang, Humla and Rasuwa touch China. Jumla does not.

questions.label: Expected – Practice
questions.stem: Which national park spreads over three provinces?
questions.explanation: Chitwan National Park lies in Chitwan and Makawanpur (Bagmati), Nawalpur (Gandaki) and Parsa (Madhesh).

topics.title: End-of-chapter test — Top 25

questions.label: Expected – Practice
questions.stem: How much area did the map of 2077 BS add to the official area of Nepal?

questions.label: Expected – Practice
questions.stem: Which Indian state does not share a boundary with Nepal?
questions.explanation: The five states are Sikkim, West Bengal, Bihar, Uttar Pradesh and Uttarakhand.

questions.label: Pattern-Based – Reconstructed
questions.stem:
Read the statements.

  1. 27 districts of Nepal touch India.
  2. 15 districts of Nepal touch China.
  3. 35 districts of Nepal touch no foreign country.

Which statements are correct?
questions.explanation: Two districts touch both neighbours, so 40 districts touch a foreign country and 37, not 35, touch none.

questions.label: Expected – Practice
questions.stem: In the five-fold physiographic division, which region has the largest share of Nepal's area?
questions.explanation: Middle Mountains 29.2%; High Himal 23.9%; High Mountains 20.4%; Terai 13.7%; Churia 12.8%.

questions.label: Expected – Practice
questions.stem: How many districts does the census classify as Mountain districts?
questions.explanation: Mountain 16, Hill 40, Terai 21.

questions.label: Pattern-Based – Reconstructed
questions.stem:
Match the peak with its district.

Peak District
A. Kanchenjunga 1. Gorkha
B. Makalu 2. Myagdi
C. Manaslu 3. Taplejung
D. Dhaulagiri 4. Sankhuwasabha
questions.explanation: Kanchenjunga–Taplejung, Makalu–Sankhuwasabha, Manaslu–Gorkha, Dhaulagiri–Myagdi.

questions.label: Expected – Practice
questions.stem: Which peak, known as "Fishtail", is not open for climbing?
questions.explanation: Machhapuchhre (6,993 m) stands in Kaski, north of Pokhara.

questions.label: Expected – Practice
questions.stem: Thorong La pass lies between which two districts?
questions.explanation: Thorong La (5,416 m) is an internal pass on the Annapurna circuit. It does not lead to Tibet.

questions.label: Expected – Practice
questions.stem: In which district is the glacial lake Tsho Rolpa?
questions.explanation: Tsho Rolpa is in Dolakha. Imja is in Solukhumbu and Thulagi is in Manang.

questions.label: Pattern-Based – Reconstructed
questions.stem:
Arrange these branches of the Gandaki from west to east.

  1. Trishuli
  2. Kali Gandaki
  3. Marsyangdi
  4. Budhi Gandaki
questions.explanation: West to east: Kali Gandaki, Seti, Madi, Marsyangdi, Daraundi, Budhi Gandaki, Trishuli.

questions.label: Expected – Practice
questions.stem: Which river is called the "Sorrow of Bihar"?
questions.explanation: The Koshi often changes its course and floods the plain of Bihar.

questions.label: Expected – Practice
questions.stem: In which year was the Mahakali Treaty between Nepal and India signed?
questions.explanation: The Koshi Agreement dates from 1954, the Gandak Agreement from 1959 and the Mahakali Treaty from 12 February 1996.

questions.label: Pattern-Based – Reconstructed
questions.stem: Which one does not belong to the group?
questions.explanation: Koshi, Karnali and Narayani are snow-fed rivers that rise in the Himalaya. The Bagmati rises in the hills north of Kathmandu.

questions.label: Expected – Practice
questions.stem: Which Ramsar site lies in Kailali district?
questions.explanation: Jagadishpur is in Kapilvastu, Bishazari in Chitwan and Mai Pokhari in Ilam.

questions.label: Pattern-Based – Reconstructed
questions.stem:
Assertion (A): The Chure hills suffer heavily from erosion and landslides.

Reason (R): The Chure hills are young and are made of loose sand, gravel and soft rock.
options: Both A and R are true, and R explains A.
Both A and R are true, but R does not explain A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.
questions.explanation: Weak rock breaks down quickly, especially where forest is cut and gravel is dug out.

questions.label: Expected – Practice
questions.stem: Lumle, the place that receives the most rain in Nepal, lies in which district?
questions.explanation: Lumle lies west of Pokhara on the southern slope of the Annapurna range.

questions.label: Pattern-Based – Reconstructed
questions.stem: Fill in the blank. In the textbook classification, the ______ belt lies between about 3,300 m and 5,000 m.
questions.explanation: Sub-tropical up to 1,200 m; warm temperate to 2,100 m; cool temperate to 3,300 m; alpine to 5,000 m; tundra above.

questions.label: Expected – Practice
questions.stem: Which is the only hunting reserve of Nepal?
questions.explanation: Dhorpatan lies in Rukum East, Baglung and Myagdi and is known for blue sheep.

questions.label: Pattern-Based – Reconstructed
questions.stem:
Match the protected area with its description.

Protected area Description
A. Annapurna 1. Smallest protected area
B. Rara 2. Only wildlife reserve
C. Krishnasar 3. Largest protected area
D. Koshi Tappu 4. Smallest national park
questions.explanation: Annapurna is the largest protected area, Rara the smallest national park, Krishnasar the smallest protected area and Koshi Tappu the only wildlife reserve.

questions.label: Expected – Practice
questions.stem: How many wild tigers did the national count announced on 29 July 2026 find in Nepal?

questions.label: Expected – Practice
questions.stem: Which province has neither a metropolitan city nor a sub-metropolitan city?
questions.explanation: Gandaki has Pokhara Metropolitan City, Sudurpashchim has Dhangadhi Sub-Metropolitan City and Lumbini has four sub-metropolitan cities.

questions.label: Pattern-Based – Reconstructed
questions.stem:
Arrange the districts by area, largest first.

  1. Bhaktapur
  2. Dolpa
  3. Kathmandu
  4. Humla
questions.explanation: Dolpa is the largest district and Humla the second largest. Bhaktapur is the smallest.

questions.label: Expected – Practice
questions.stem: Which province has the largest number of municipalities (नगरपालिका)?
questions.explanation: Madhesh has 73 municipalities. Koshi has the most rural municipalities (88).

questions.label: Pattern-Based – Reconstructed
questions.stem:
Read the statements.

  1. Kulekhani is a storage-type hydropower project.
  2. Most hydropower stations of Nepal are run-of-river stations.
  3. Run-of-river stations produce the most power in the dry winter.

Which statements are correct?
questions.explanation: Run-of-river stations depend on the river's flow, so they produce the least in the dry winter.

questions.label: Expected – Practice
questions.stem: The Dhalkebar sub-station, the Nepal end of the 400 kV cross-border line to Muzaffarpur, lies in which district?
questions.explanation: Dhalkebar is in Dhanusha district of Madhesh Province.

topics.title: Sources of history and the ancient period (इतिहासका स्रोत र प्राचीन काल)

questions.label: Expected – Practice
questions.stem: Who is named as the first king of the Kirat dynasty?
questions.explanation: Yalambar was the first Kirat king and Gasti the last.

questions.label: Pattern-Based – Reconstructed
questions.stem:
Arrange the dynasties in the order in which they ruled the Kathmandu Valley.

  1. Kirat
  2. Gopal
  3. Lichhavi
  4. Mahispal
questions.explanation: Gopal, Mahispal, Kirat, then (after the short Soma dynasty) Lichhavi.

questions.label: Pattern-Based – Reconstructed
questions.stem:
Match List I with List II.

List I List II
A. Changu Narayan pillar 1. Coin
B. Lumbini pillar 2. Chronicle
C. Gopal Raj Vamshavali 3. Inscription of Manadeva
D. Mananka 4. Inscription of Ashoka
questions.explanation: The Changu Narayan pillar carries Manadeva's inscription, the Lumbini pillar Ashoka's; the Gopal Raj Vamshavali is a chronicle and the Mananka a coin.

questions.label: Pattern-Based – Reconstructed
questions.stem:
Read the statements.

  1. Ashoka set up the pillar at Lumbini in 249 BC.
  2. The Lumbini inscription is written in the Brahmi script.
  3. Lumbini was placed on the World Heritage List in 1979.

Which statements are correct?
questions.explanation: Lumbini was listed in 1997.

questions.label: Expected – Practice
questions.stem: According to tradition, Gautam Buddha visited the Kathmandu Valley during the reign of which Kirat king?
questions.explanation: Jitedasti was the 7th Kirat king. Tradition places Ashoka's visit in the time of Sthunko, the 14th.

topics.title: Lichhavi period (लिच्छविकाल)

questions.label: Expected – Practice
questions.stem: Which Lichhavi king issued the coin called Mananka?
questions.explanation: The Mananka of Manadeva is regarded as the first coin of Nepal.

questions.label: Pattern-Based – Reconstructed
questions.stem:
Match the palace with the ruler who is linked with it.

Palace Ruler
A. Managriha 1. Narendradeva
B. Kailashkut Bhawan 2. Manadeva
C. Bhadradhivas 3. Amshuverma
questions.explanation: Managriha–Manadeva, Kailashkut Bhawan–Amshuverma, Bhadradhivas–Narendradeva.

questions.label: Pattern-Based – Reconstructed
questions.stem: Which one does not belong to the group?
questions.explanation: The first three are Lichhavi palaces. Hanuman Dhoka is the Malla and Shah palace of Kathmandu.

questions.label: Pattern-Based – Reconstructed
questions.stem:
Read the statements.

  1. The Lichhavis came to Nepal from Vaishali.
  2. Amshuverma wrote Shabda Vidya.
  3. The Changu Narayan pillar inscription was set up by Amshuverma.

Which statements are correct?
questions.explanation: The Changu Narayan inscription (464 AD) was set up by Manadeva.

questions.label: Expected – Practice
questions.stem: In the Lichhavi period, the tax on farm produce was called:
questions.explanation: Bhaga was the tax on farm produce, bhoga on animals and kara on trade. Vishti was unpaid labour.

topics.title: Medieval period (मध्यकाल)

questions.label: Expected – Practice
questions.stem: Who built the stone Krishna Mandir of Patan?
questions.explanation: Siddhi Narsingh Malla of Lalitpur built it in 1637.

questions.label: Pattern-Based – Reconstructed
questions.stem:
Match the kingdom with its last Malla king.

Kingdom Last king
A. Kantipur 1. Ranajit Malla
B. Lalitpur 2. Jaya Prakash Malla
C. Bhaktapur 3. Tej Narsingh Malla
questions.explanation: Jaya Prakash Malla (Kantipur), Tej Narsingh Malla (Lalitpur), Ranajit Malla (Bhaktapur).

questions.label: Pattern-Based – Reconstructed
questions.stem:
Read the statements about the Khas kingdom.

  1. Dullu was its summer capital.
  2. Its capital, Sinja, lies in today's Jumla district.
  3. The name of Ripu Malla is cut on the Ashoka pillar at Lumbini.

Which statements are correct?
questions.explanation: Statement 1 is wrong: Dullu, in Dailekh, was the winter capital.

questions.label: Expected – Practice
questions.stem: Simraungadh, the capital of the Karnat dynasty, lies in which present-day district?
questions.explanation: Simraungadh is in Bara district of Madhesh Province. Nanyadeva founded the dynasty in 1097 AD.

questions.label: Pattern-Based – Reconstructed
questions.stem:
Assertion (A): After the death of Yaksha Malla the Kathmandu Valley was divided into separate kingdoms.

Reason (R): Jayasthiti Malla divided society into classes and castes by occupation.
options: Both A and R are true, and R explains A.
Both A and R are true, but R does not explain A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.
questions.explanation: Both statements are true, but the kingdom was divided among Yaksha Malla's heirs. The social reform of Jayasthiti Malla, a century earlier, was not the cause.

topics.title: Unification to the Sugauli Treaty (एकीकरणदेखि सुगौली सन्धिसम्म)

questions.label: Expected – Practice
questions.stem: Which was the first place won by Prithvi Narayan Shah in his unification campaign?
questions.explanation: Nuwakot was won in 1744 (1801 BS), after a failed attack in 1743.
