D. Clause (5) 4. Member who commands a majority with the support of two or more parties
questions.explanation: Majority party, then coalition, then largest party, then any member who can show support.

questions.label: Pattern-Based – Reconstructed
questions.stem:
Read the statements.

  1. A person who is not a member of the Federal Parliament can never be appointed a minister.
  2. The Council of Ministers may have at most 25 members, including the Prime Minister.
  3. The executive power of Nepal lies in the Council of Ministers.

Which statements are correct?
questions.explanation: Under Article 78 a non-member may be appointed, but must become a member of the Federal Parliament within six months.

questions.label: Pattern-Based – Reconstructed
questions.stem:
Arrange these Presidents of Nepal in order of time, earliest first.

  1. Bidya Devi Bhandari
  2. Ram Chandra Paudel
  3. Ram Baran Yadav
questions.explanation: Ram Baran Yadav (2065), Bidya Devi Bhandari (2072), Ram Chandra Paudel (2079).

topics.title: Federal Parliament and law-making (संघीय संसद र कानून निर्माण)

questions.label: Expected – Practice
questions.stem: How many members does the Federal Parliament of Nepal have in all?
questions.explanation: 275 in the House of Representatives and 59 in the National Assembly.

questions.label: Expected – Practice
questions.stem: What is the term of office of a member of the National Assembly?
questions.explanation: Six years. One-third of the members retire every two years, so the House itself is permanent.

questions.label: Pattern-Based – Reconstructed
questions.stem:
Match the event with its time limit.

Event Time limit
A. National Assembly returns a Money Bill 1. Six months
B. National Assembly returns any other Bill 2. Sixty days
C. An Ordinance lapses after both Houses meet 3. Fifteen days
D. Longest gap between two sessions 4. Two months
questions.explanation: Fifteen days, two months, sixty days, six months.

questions.label: Pattern-Based – Reconstructed
questions.stem:
Read the statements.

  1. The quorum of each House is one-fourth of its total members.
  2. The yearly budget estimate is presented on Jestha 15.
  3. A Money Bill may be introduced in either House.

Which statements are correct?
questions.explanation: A Money Bill may be introduced only in the House of Representatives (Article 110).

questions.label: Pattern-Based – Reconstructed
questions.stem:
Arrange the steps by which a Bill becomes an Act, first step first.

  1. The President authenticates the Bill.
  2. The Bill is introduced in one House.
  3. The second House passes the Bill.
  4. The first House passes the Bill.
questions.explanation: Introduction, passage by the first House, passage by the second House, authentication.

topics.title: Judiciary (न्यायपालिका)

questions.label: Expected – Practice
questions.stem: Besides the Chief Justice, what is the largest number of judges the Supreme Court may have?
questions.explanation: Article 129: at most twenty judges in addition to the Chief Justice.

questions.label: Expected – Practice
questions.stem: Who appoints the Chief Judge and the judges of a High Court?
options: The President, on the recommendation of the Constitutional Council
The Province Chief, on the recommendation of the Chief Minister
The President, on the recommendation of the Judicial Council
The Chief Justice, on the recommendation of the Judicial Council
questions.explanation: Article 140. The same rule applies to District Judges (Article 149).

questions.label: Pattern-Based – Reconstructed
questions.stem:
Match the writ with its purpose.

Writ Purpose
A. Habeas corpus 1. To ask by what authority a person holds a public office
B. Mandamus 2. To cancel an unlawful decision
C. Certiorari 3. To free a person held unlawfully
D. Quo warranto 4. To order an authority to do its legal duty
questions.explanation: Habeas corpus frees a person; mandamus commands a duty; certiorari cancels a decision; quo warranto questions the right to an office.

questions.label: Pattern-Based – Reconstructed
questions.stem: Three of these are members of the Judicial Council. Which one is not?
options: The Federal Minister for Law and Justice
The senior-most judge of the Supreme Court
questions.explanation: The Attorney General is a member of the Judicial Service Commission (Article 154), not of the Judicial Council (Article 153).

questions.label: Pattern-Based – Reconstructed
questions.stem:
Read the statements.

  1. A judge of the Supreme Court retires at the age of 65.
  2. A judge of a High Court retires at the age of 65.
  3. The Constitutional Bench consists of the Chief Justice and four other judges.

Which statements are correct?
questions.explanation: Judges of High Courts and District Courts retire at 63.

topics.title: Constitutional bodies (संवैधानिक निकाय)

questions.label: Expected – Practice
questions.stem: How many bodies does Article 306 of the Constitution name as "constitutional bodies"?
questions.explanation: Thirteen: six in Parts 21 to 26 and seven commissions in Part 27.

questions.label: Expected – Practice
questions.stem: Who chairs the Constitutional Council?
options: The Speaker of the House of Representatives
questions.explanation: Article 284. The Chief Justice and the Speaker are members.

questions.label: Pattern-Based – Reconstructed
questions.stem:
Match the constitutional body with the Part of the Constitution that sets it up.

Body Part
A. Commission for the Investigation of Abuse of Authority 1. Part 24
B. Auditor General 2. Part 23
C. Public Service Commission 3. Part 21
D. Election Commission 4. Part 22
questions.explanation: Parts 21, 22, 23 and 24, in that order.

questions.label: Pattern-Based – Reconstructed
questions.stem: Three of these are constitutional bodies under Article 306. Which one is not?
options: National Natural Resources and Fiscal Commission
questions.explanation: The Language Commission is formed by the Government of Nepal under Article 287 and is not on the Article 306 list.

questions.label: Pattern-Based – Reconstructed
questions.stem:
Read the statements.

  1. The term of office in the constitutional bodies is five years.
  2. A member of the Public Service Commission must hold at least a master's degree.
  3. The Commission for the Investigation of Abuse of Authority has a Chief Commissioner and four other Commissioners.

Which statements are correct?
questions.explanation: The term is six years from the date of appointment.

topics.title: Emergency powers, amendment procedure and amendments so far (संकटकालीन अधिकार, संविधान संशोधन र हालसम्मका संशोधन)

questions.label: Expected – Practice
questions.stem: Which Article of the Constitution lays down the procedure for amending it?
questions.explanation: Article 274, the only Article of Part 31. Article 273 is on emergency power and Article 275 on referendum.

questions.label: Expected – Practice
questions.stem: Once both Houses approve it, for how long does a declaration of emergency stay in force, counted from the date it was issued?
questions.explanation: Three months. It may be extended once, for up to three months more.

questions.label: Pattern-Based – Reconstructed
questions.stem:
Read the statements.

  1. The first amendment changed Articles 42, 84 and 286.
  2. The second amendment changed the coat of arms in Schedule 3.
  3. The second amendment was made in 2072 BS.

Which statements are correct?
questions.explanation: The second amendment was made in 2077 BS. The first amendment was made in 2072 BS.

questions.label: Pattern-Based – Reconstructed
questions.stem:
Assertion (A): A Bill to amend the Constitution must be passed by at least two-thirds of all members of both Houses of the Federal Parliament.

Reason (R): Clause (1) of Article 274 cannot itself be amended.
options: Both A and R are true, and R explains A.
Both A and R are true, but R does not explain A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.
questions.explanation: Both are rules of Article 274, but they are separate. One sets the majority; the other protects sovereignty and territorial integrity from amendment.

questions.label: Pattern-Based – Reconstructed
questions.stem: Three of these are grounds for a state of emergency under Article 273. Which one is not?
options: Defeat of the government in a vote of confidence
questions.explanation: The six grounds are war, external aggression, armed rebellion, extreme economic disarray, natural calamity and epidemic. Losing a vote of confidence leads to a change of government under Articles 76 and 100.

topics.title: End-of-chapter test — Top 25

questions.label: Expected – Practice
questions.stem: Which Article declares the Constitution to be the fundamental law of Nepal?
questions.explanation: Article 1. Article 2 is on sovereignty, Article 4 on the State of Nepal, and Article 307 on the short title and commencement.

questions.label: Expected – Practice
questions.stem: Which Article makes Nepali in the Devanagari script the official language of Nepal?
questions.explanation: Article 7. Article 6 says that all mother tongues spoken in Nepal are languages of the nation.

questions.label: Expected – Practice
questions.stem: Who chaired the Constituent Assembly that passed the Constitution of Nepal?
questions.explanation: Subas Chandra Nembang. Krishna Prasad Sitaula chaired the Drafting Committee; Ram Baran Yadav, as President, proclaimed the Constitution.

questions.label: Pattern-Based – Reconstructed
questions.stem:
Arrange these constitutions by the number of their Articles, fewest first.

  1. Interim Constitution of Nepal, 2063
  2. Constitution of the Kingdom of Nepal, 2047
  3. Constitution of Nepal (2072)
  4. Constitution of Nepal, 2019
questions.explanation: 97, 133, 167 and 308 Articles.

questions.label: Expected – Practice
questions.stem: Which Article fixes Kathmandu as the capital of Nepal?
questions.explanation: Article 288. The same Article lets a Provincial Assembly choose the provincial capital by a two-thirds majority.

questions.label: Expected – Practice
questions.stem: How many items are there in Schedule 5, the list of federal powers?
questions.explanation: Thirty-five. Schedule 6 has 21, Schedule 7 has 25, Schedule 8 has 22 and Schedule 9 has 15.

questions.label: Expected – Practice
questions.stem: Under Article 58, which level of government holds the residual powers?
options: The federation and the provinces jointly
questions.explanation: Any matter not placed in a list belongs to the federation.

questions.label: Pattern-Based – Reconstructed
questions.stem:
Match the right with its Article.

Right Article
A. Right to equality 1. Article 44
B. Right to privacy 2. Article 38
C. Rights of women 3. Article 18
D. Rights of the consumer 4. Article 28
questions.explanation: Equality 18, privacy 28, women 38, consumer 44.

questions.label: Expected – Practice
questions.stem: Which Article gives the right to constitutional remedy?
questions.explanation: Article 46, used through Article 133 (Supreme Court) or Article 144 (High Court).

questions.label: Expected – Practice
questions.stem: Up to which level does Article 31 make education both compulsory and free?
questions.explanation: Compulsory and free up to the basic level; free up to the secondary level.

questions.label: Pattern-Based – Reconstructed
questions.stem: Fill in the blanks. The President of Nepal holds office for ______ years, and a person may be elected President at most ______ times.
questions.explanation: Articles 63 and 64.

questions.label: Expected – Practice
questions.stem: Who performs the functions of the President if the offices of both President and Vice-President fall vacant?
options: The Chairperson of the National Assembly
The Speaker of the House of Representatives
questions.explanation: Article 280.

questions.label: Expected – Practice
questions.stem: Before whom does the President of Nepal take the oath of office?
options: The Speaker of the House of Representatives
questions.explanation: Article 71. The Vice-President takes the oath before the President.

questions.label: Pattern-Based – Reconstructed
questions.stem:
Read the statements about a motion of no-confidence against the Prime Minister.

  1. It is tabled by one-fourth of the members of the House of Representatives.
  2. It may be tabled in the first year after the Prime Minister's appointment.
  3. It must name the member proposed as the next Prime Minister.

Which statements are correct?
questions.explanation: Under Article 100 the motion cannot be tabled in the first two years after the appointment.

questions.label: Expected – Practice
questions.stem: What is the minimum age for membership of the National Assembly?
questions.explanation: Thirty-five. For the House of Representatives it is 25.

questions.label: Expected – Practice
questions.stem: How many members of the National Assembly are nominated by the President?
questions.explanation: Three, on the recommendation of the Government of Nepal; at least one must be a woman.

questions.label: Expected – Practice
questions.stem: Within how many days must the President authenticate a Bill presented under Article 113?
questions.explanation: Fifteen days. Within that time the President may instead return a Bill once, but not a Money Bill.

questions.label: Pattern-Based – Reconstructed
questions.stem: Three of these courts are named in Article 127 of the Constitution. Which one is not?
questions.explanation: The Appellate Courts were replaced by the High Courts under this Constitution.

questions.label: Expected – Practice
questions.stem: On whose recommendation does the President appoint the Attorney General?
questions.explanation: Article 157. The Attorney General holds office as long as the Prime Minister wishes.

questions.label: Expected – Practice
questions.stem: What is the term of office of the Chief Justice of Nepal?
questions.explanation: Article 129. The Chief Justice must still retire on reaching 65.

questions.label: Pattern-Based – Reconstructed
questions.stem:
Assertion (A): A Money Bill can be introduced only in the House of Representatives.

Reason (R): The National Assembly has no power to discuss a Money Bill.
options: Both A and R are true, and R explains A.
Both A and R are true, but R does not explain A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.
questions.explanation: The National Assembly does discuss a Money Bill and returns it within fifteen days, with suggestions if any.

questions.label: Expected – Practice
questions.stem: Which body holds a referendum under the Constitution?
questions.explanation: Article 246. The decision to hold one is taken by two-thirds of the Federal Parliament (Article 275).

questions.label: Expected – Practice
questions.stem: How many members, including the chairperson, has the National Security Council?
questions.explanation: The Prime Minister, four ministers (Defence, Home, Foreign Affairs, Finance), the Chief Secretary and the Chief of the Army Staff.

questions.label: Pattern-Based – Reconstructed
questions.stem:
Arrange the events in order of time, earliest first.

  1. Second amendment of the Constitution
  2. Proclamation of the Constitution
  3. First amendment of the Constitution
  4. First election of the House of Representatives under the Constitution
questions.explanation: Ashoj 2072, Magh 2072, Mangsir 2074, Ashad 2077.

questions.label: Expected – Practice
questions.stem: 🔄 Under which clause of Article 76 was Balendra Shah appointed Prime Minister on 13 Chaitra 2082?
questions.explanation: Clause (1): leader of a parliamentary party with a majority in the House of Representatives.

topics.title: Three tiers of government and Schedules 5 to 9 (तीन तहको सरकार र अनुसूची ५ देखि ९)

questions.label: Expected – Practice
questions.stem: Which Article of the Constitution says that the State has three levels — Federation, Province and Local level?
questions.explanation: Article 56 (1), in Part 5, sets out the three-level structure. Article 232 deals with relations among the levels.

questions.label: Pattern-Based – Reconstructed
questions.stem:
Match the Schedule with its list.

  1. Schedule 5 — A. Local level powers
  2. Schedule 6 — B. Concurrent powers of the Federation and the Province
  3. Schedule 7 — C. Federal powers
  4. Schedule 8 — D. Provincial powers
questions.explanation: Schedule 5 is federal, 6 provincial, 7 shared by the Federation and the Province, and 8 local. Schedule 9 is shared by all three.

questions.label: Expected – Practice
questions.stem: A new subject — for example, the regulation of artificial intelligence — is not named in any of the five lists in Schedules 5 to 9. Under the Constitution, which level may make law on it?
options: The Province in which the matter arises
The Federation and the Province jointly
questions.explanation: A subject that no list names is a residual power, and Article 58 gives residual power to the Federation.

questions.label: Pattern-Based – Reconstructed
questions.stem:
Consider these statements.

  1. The District Assembly is part of the local level.
  2. Schedule 9 has 15 items.
  3. Basic and secondary education is in the federal list.

Which of them are correct?
questions.explanation: Statements 1 and 2 are correct (Article 56 (4); Schedule 9). Basic and secondary education is in Schedule 8, the local list.

questions.label: Pattern-Based – Reconstructed
questions.stem: Three of these are in the federal list (Schedule 5). Which one is not?
questions.explanation: Management of trusts is item 21 of the provincial list (Schedule 6).

topics.title: Provincial executive, Provincial Assembly and provincial institutions (प्रदेश कार्यपालिका, प्रदेश सभा र प्रदेशका संस्था)

questions.label: Expected – Practice
questions.stem: Who appoints the Province Chief?
questions.explanation: Article 163 (2): the President appoints one Province Chief for each province.

questions.label: Expected – Practice
questions.stem: What is the largest size allowed for a Provincial Council of Ministers?
options: Twenty percent of the total members of the Provincial Assembly, including the Chief Minister
Twenty-five members, including the Chief Minister
Ten percent of the total members of the Provincial Assembly
Fifteen percent of the members, not counting the Chief Minister
questions.explanation: Article 168 (9). The limit of 25 applies to the federal Council of Ministers.

questions.label: Pattern-Based – Reconstructed
questions.stem:
Consider these statements.

  1. A Provincial Assembly has one house.
  2. A member of a Provincial Assembly must be at least 25 years old.
  3. A Province Chief must be at least 35 years old.

Which of them are correct?
questions.explanation: All three are correct (Articles 175, 178 and 164).

questions.label: Pattern-Based – Reconstructed
questions.stem: Fill in the blank. A Chief Minister appointed under Article 168 (2) must obtain a vote of confidence from the Provincial Assembly within ______ days of appointment.
questions.explanation: Article 168 (4) gives 30 days. Thirty-five days is the limit for the whole process of appointing a Chief Minister.

questions.label: Pattern-Based – Reconstructed
questions.stem:
Match the office with its role.

  1. Province Chief — A. Chief legal adviser of the Provincial Government
  2. Chief Minister — B. Representative of the Government of Nepal in the province
  3. Chief Attorney — C. Head of the Provincial Council of Ministers
  4. Speaker — D. Presides over the Provincial Assembly
questions.explanation: Articles 163, 168, 160 and 182.

topics.title: Local government: structure, powers and the Local Government Operation Act (स्थानीय सरकार: संरचना, अधिकार र स्थानीय सरकार सञ्चालन ऐन, २०७४)

questions.label: Expected – Practice
questions.stem: Who coordinates the Judicial Committee of a municipality?
questions.explanation: Article 217: the Deputy Mayor in a municipality and the Vice-Chairperson in a rural municipality.

questions.label: Expected – Practice
questions.stem: What is the largest number of members a District Coordination Committee may have?
questions.explanation: Article 220 (3): at most nine, including the Chief and the Deputy Chief.

questions.label: Pattern-Based – Reconstructed
questions.stem: Which of these statements is not correct?
options: A Ward Committee has a chairperson and four members.
The term of a Village Assembly and a Municipal Assembly is five years.
A Municipal Executive includes four women members elected by the Municipal Assembly.
A candidate for a local post must be at least 21 years old.
questions.explanation: A Municipal Executive includes five women members (Article 216). Four is the number for a Village Executive.

questions.label: Pattern-Based – Reconstructed
questions.stem:
Arrange the types of local level from the most numerous to the least numerous.

  1. Metropolitan cities
  2. Rural municipalities
  3. Sub-metropolitan cities
  4. Municipalities
questions.explanation: Rural municipalities 460, municipalities 276, sub-metropolitan cities 11, metropolitan cities 6.

questions.label: Expected – Practice
questions.stem: Under the Local Government Operation Act, 2074, how many permanent residents must a town have, at the least, to become a sub-metropolitan city?
questions.explanation: Two hundred thousand (2 lakh). Five hundred thousand is the figure for a metropolitan city.

topics.title: Inter-governmental relations and fiscal federalism (अन्तर-सरकारी सम्बन्ध र वित्तीय संघीयता)

questions.label: Expected – Practice
questions.stem: Who chairs the Inter-Province Council under Article 234?
options: The Chairperson of the National Assembly
questions.explanation: The Prime Minister chairs it; the Home Minister, the Finance Minister and the Chief Ministers concerned are members.

questions.label: Pattern-Based – Reconstructed
questions.stem: Fill in the blank. Value-added tax and excise on domestic products are shared among the Federation, the provinces and the local levels in the ratio ______.
questions.explanation: 70 : 15 : 15 under the Inter-Governmental Fiscal Arrangement Act, 2074. The ratio 50 : 25 : 25 is for royalty from natural resources.

questions.label: Pattern-Based – Reconstructed
questions.stem:
Match the grant with its description.

  1. Fiscal equalisation grant — A. Matching money for infrastructure projects
  2. Conditional grant — B. Based on the need for spending and the capacity to raise revenue
  3. Complementary grant — C. Tied to a named programme or standard
  4. Special grant — D. For a specific purpose such as basic services or the uplift of disadvantaged groups
questions.explanation: Equalisation follows need and capacity; conditional is tied; complementary is matching money; special is for a specific purpose.

questions.label: Expected – Practice
questions.stem: Which body recommends the fiscal equalisation grants to be given to the provinces and local levels?
options: The National Natural Resources and Fiscal Commission
questions.explanation: Articles 60 (3) and 251 (1)(b).

questions.label: Pattern-Based – Reconstructed
questions.stem:
Consider these statements.

  1. Only the Government of Nepal may take foreign loans.
  2. Royalty from natural resources is shared 50 : 25 : 25.
  3. Local levels present their budget by 10 Ashad.

Which of them are correct?
questions.explanation: All three are correct (Article 59 (6) and the Inter-Governmental Fiscal Arrangement Act, 2074).

topics.title: Elections and the political system (निर्वाचन र राजनीतिक प्रणाली)

questions.label: Expected – Practice
questions.stem: How is the Election Commission of Nepal composed?
options: A Chief Election Commissioner and two Commissioners
A Chief Election Commissioner and four Commissioners
A Chief Election Commissioner and five Commissioners
A Chief Election Commissioner and six Commissioners
questions.explanation: Article 245 (1): five members in all.

questions.label: Expected – Practice
questions.stem: What share of the valid proportional votes must a party win to receive proportional seats in the House of Representatives?
questions.explanation: Three percent. The figure of 1.5 percent applies to Provincial Assemblies.

questions.label: Pattern-Based – Reconstructed
questions.stem:
Arrange these elections in order of time, earliest first.

  1. First phase of the first local elections under the present Constitution
  2. Election to the House of Representatives after the Gen Z movement
  3. Second local elections under the present Constitution
  4. First elections to the Provincial Assemblies
questions.explanation: Baisakh 2074, Mangsir 2074, Baisakh 2079, Falgun 2082.

questions.label: Pattern-Based – Reconstructed
questions.stem:
Consider these statements.

  1. Local elections use only the first-past-the-post system.
  2. A national party needs 3 percent of the proportional votes and at least one first-past-the-post seat in the House of Representatives.
  3. All members of a Provincial Assembly are elected by proportional representation.

Which of them are correct?
questions.explanation: Statement 3 is wrong: 60 percent of a Provincial Assembly is elected by first-past-the-post and 40 percent by proportional representation.

questions.label: Pattern-Based – Reconstructed
questions.stem: Three of these elections are conducted by the Election Commission. Which one is not?
options: Election of the Speaker of the House of Representatives
Election of members of a Provincial Assembly
questions.explanation: The House elects its own Speaker. Article 246 gives the Commission the elections of the President, Vice-President, Parliament, Provincial Assemblies and local levels.

topics.title: Civil service and the Public Service Commissions (निजामती सेवा र लोक सेवा आयोग)

questions.label: Expected – Practice
questions.stem: Which Article of the Constitution provides for a Province Public Service Commission?
questions.explanation: Article 244. Articles 242 and 243 deal with the federal Commission; Article 285 with forming government services.

questions.label: Expected – Practice
questions.stem: Of the posts set aside for inclusion in the civil service, what share goes to women?
questions.explanation: Thirty-three percent of the reserved share. Forty-five percent is the reserved share itself.

questions.label: Pattern-Based – Reconstructed
questions.stem:
Match the head of administrative staff with the level.

  1. Chief Secretary — A. Local level
  2. Principal Secretary — B. Federation
  3. Chief Administrative Officer — C. Province
questions.explanation: Chief Secretary: Federation; Principal Secretary: province; Chief Administrative Officer: local level.

questions.label: Pattern-Based – Reconstructed
questions.stem:
Consider these statements about the federal Public Service Commission.

  1. It has a Chairperson and four members.
  2. The term of office is six years.
  3. It conducts the written examination for appointment to the Nepal Police.

Which of them are correct?
questions.explanation: All three are correct (Articles 242 and 243).

questions.label: Pattern-Based – Reconstructed
questions.stem: Assertion (A): Every province of Nepal has its own Public Service Commission. Reason (R): Article 244 provides for a Province Public Service Commission in each province, on standards fixed by federal law.
options: Both A and R are true, but R does not explain A.
Both A and R are true, and R explains A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.
questions.explanation: The seven Commissions exist because Article 244 requires one in each province.

topics.title: Good governance, right to information and control of corruption (सुशासन, सूचनाको हक र भ्रष्टाचार नियन्त्रण)

questions.label: Expected – Practice
questions.stem: Which Article of the Constitution guarantees the right to information?
questions.explanation: Article 27. Article 17 is the right to freedom, Article 19 the right to communication and Article 25 the right to property.

questions.label: Expected – Practice
questions.stem: Under the Right to Information Act, 2064, if information cannot be given at once, within how many days must it be given?
questions.explanation: Fifteen days. Seven days is for the complaint to the head of the office, and 35 days for the appeal to the Commission.

questions.label: Pattern-Based – Reconstructed
questions.stem:
Match the body with its work.

  1. Commission for the Investigation of Abuse of Authority — A. Tries corruption cases
  2. Special Court — B. Preventive body under the Prime Minister's supervision
  3. National Vigilance Centre — C. Investigates corruption and files cases
  4. National Information Commission — D. Hears appeals when information is refused
questions.explanation: The Commission investigates, the Special Court tries, the Vigilance Centre prevents and the Information Commission hears appeals.

questions.label: Pattern-Based – Reconstructed
questions.stem:
Consider these statements.

  1. The Good Governance (Management and Operation) Act, 2064 requires offices serving the public to display a citizen charter.
  2. The National Information Commission has a Chief Information Commissioner and four Commissioners.
  3. Nepal scored 34 in the Corruption Perceptions Index 2025.

Which of them are correct?
questions.explanation: Statement 2 is wrong: the Commission has a Chief Information Commissioner and two Commissioners.

questions.label: Pattern-Based – Reconstructed
questions.stem: Three of these are accepted signs of good governance. Which one is not?
questions.explanation: Good governance calls for openness. Only information that the law protects may be kept secret.

topics.title: Electronic governance and public service delivery (विद्युतीय सुशासन र सार्वजनिक सेवा प्रवाह)

questions.label: Expected – Practice
questions.stem: Which law gives legal recognition to electronic records and digital signatures in Nepal?
questions.explanation: The Electronic Transactions Act, 2063.

questions.label: Expected – Practice
questions.stem: How many sectors and initiatives does the Digital Nepal Framework, 2076 contain?
questions.explanation: Eight sectors and eighty initiatives.

questions.label: Pattern-Based – Reconstructed
questions.stem:
Match the kind of e-governance link with the example.

  1. G2C — A. One ministry shares its records with another
  2. G2B — B. A citizen applies for a driving licence online
  3. G2G — C. A firm submits a bid through the electronic procurement portal
  4. G2E — D. An employee checks a pay record online
questions.explanation: Citizen, business, government and employee in that order.

questions.label: Pattern-Based – Reconstructed
questions.stem:
Consider these statements.

  1. Distribution of the National Identity Card began in Panchthar district.
  2. The toll-free number of Hello Sarkar is 1111.
  3. The Nagarik App was launched before the Electronic Transactions Act was made.

Which of them are correct?
questions.explanation: Statement 3 is wrong: the Act is of 2063 BS and the App was launched in 2077 BS.

questions.label: Pattern-Based – Reconstructed
questions.stem: Three of these are expected benefits of e-governance. Which one is not?
questions.explanation: E-governance is meant to remove middlemen, not add them.

topics.title: End-of-chapter test — Top 25

questions.label: Expected – Practice
questions.stem: Which Part of the Constitution deals with the structure of the State and the distribution of State power?
questions.explanation: Part 5, Articles 56 to 60. Part 20 deals with relations among the three levels.

questions.label: Expected – Practice
questions.stem: How many items are there in the provincial list (Schedule 6)?
questions.explanation: Twenty-one. The other figures belong to Schedules 5, 7 and 8.

questions.label: Pattern-Based – Reconstructed
questions.stem:
Match the subject with the Schedule in which it appears.

  1. Town police — A. Schedule 5
  2. Provincial highways — B. Schedule 6
  3. Casino and lottery — C. Schedule 7
  4. Foreign and diplomatic affairs — D. Schedule 8
questions.explanation: Town police is local, provincial highways provincial, casino and lottery shared by the Federation and the Province, and foreign affairs federal.

questions.label: Expected – Practice
questions.stem: How many governments are there in Nepal when all three levels are counted?
questions.explanation: One federal, seven provincial and 753 local governments.

questions.label: Pattern-Based – Reconstructed
questions.stem:
Consider these statements about the Province Chief.

  1. The term of office is five years.
  2. A person cannot be Province Chief twice in the same province.
  3. The Province Chief is elected by the Provincial Assembly.

Which of them are correct?
questions.explanation: The Province Chief is appointed by the President, not elected (Article 163).

questions.label: Expected – Practice
questions.stem: Within how many days must the Province Chief give assent to a Bill passed by the Provincial Assembly?
questions.explanation: Article 201 (2): fifteen days.

questions.label: Expected – Practice
questions.stem: Who appoints the Chief Attorney of a province?
options: The President, on the recommendation of the Attorney General
The Province Chief, on the recommendation of the Chief Minister
questions.explanation: Article 160 (2).

questions.label: Pattern-Based – Reconstructed
questions.stem: Fill in the blank. The number of first-past-the-post seats in a Provincial Assembly is ______ the number of House of Representatives constituencies in that province.
questions.explanation: Article 176 (1)(a). Koshi, for example, has 28 House constituencies and 56 such seats.

questions.label: Expected – Practice
questions.stem: Which members does the Village Assembly add to a Village Executive?
options: Five women and three members from Dalit or minority communities
Three women and two members from Dalit or minority communities
Four women and two members from Dalit or minority communities
Two women and one member from Dalit or minority communities
questions.explanation: Article 215 (4). Five and three is the rule for a Municipal Executive.

questions.label: Expected – Practice
questions.stem: In which year BS was the Local Government Operation Act made?
questions.explanation: It was authenticated on 29 Ashoj 2074.

questions.label: Expected – Practice
questions.stem: Who are the members of a District Assembly?
options: All ward chairpersons of the district
Members of the Provincial Assembly elected from the district
The Chief District Officer and the heads of government offices
The Chairpersons and Vice-Chairpersons of the rural municipalities and the Mayors and Deputy Mayors of the municipalities in the district
questions.explanation: Article 220 (2).

questions.label: Pattern-Based – Reconstructed
questions.stem:
Consider these statements about Article 232.

  1. Relations among the three levels rest on cooperation, coexistence and coordination.
  2. In certain grave situations the President may suspend or dissolve a Provincial Council of Ministers and Provincial Assembly for up to six months.
  3. Such a suspension or dissolution needs no approval from the Federal Parliament.

Which of them are correct?
questions.explanation: The action must be ratified by the Federal Parliament within 35 days; otherwise it lapses.

questions.label: Expected – Practice
questions.stem: In what ratio is royalty from natural resources shared among the Federation, the province concerned and the local level concerned?

questions.label: Expected – Practice
questions.stem: What is the largest number of members, including the Chairperson, of the National Natural Resources and Fiscal Commission?
questions.explanation: Article 250 (1).

questions.label: Pattern-Based – Reconstructed
questions.stem:
Match the level of government with the day by which its yearly budget is presented.

  1. Federation — A. 10 Ashad
  2. Province — B. 15 Jestha
  3. Local level — C. 1 Ashad
questions.explanation: Federation 15 Jestha, province 1 Ashad, local level 10 Ashad.

questions.label: Expected – Practice
questions.stem: In what ratio is vehicle tax shared between a province and its local levels?
questions.explanation: The province collects it and keeps 60 percent; 40 percent goes to the local levels.

questions.label: Expected – Practice
questions.stem: On which date AD was the election to the House of Representatives of 21 Falgun 2082 held?
questions.explanation: 5 March 2026. The other dates are the elections of 2079 and the swearing-in of the Prime Minister.

questions.label: Expected – Practice
questions.stem: How many parties gained the status of national party from the House of Representatives election of 2082 BS?
questions.explanation: Six. There were five after 2074 and seven after 2079.

questions.label: Expected – Practice
questions.stem: Within what period after the end of the term of the local Assemblies must the next local election be held?
questions.explanation: Article 225.

questions.label: Expected – Practice
questions.stem: When was the Public Service Commission of Nepal founded?

questions.label: Pattern-Based – Reconstructed
questions.stem:
Arrange these groups by their share of the reserved posts in the civil service, largest first.

  1. Dalit
  2. Women
  3. Madhesi
  4. Adivasi Janajati
questions.explanation: Women 33, Adivasi Janajati 27, Madhesi 22, Dalit 9.

questions.label: Expected – Practice
questions.stem: Which Article requires a federal Act for forming and running the federal civil service?
questions.explanation: Article 285 (1).

questions.label: Expected – Practice
questions.stem: Who chairs the committee that recommends the Chief Information Commissioner?
options: The Speaker of the House of Representatives
questions.explanation: The Speaker chairs it; the Minister and the head of the Federation of Nepali Journalists are members.

questions.label: Pattern-Based – Reconstructed
questions.stem: Assertion (A): A citizen charter supports good governance. Reason (R): It tells the service-seeker the service, the time, the fee and the responsible officer, so that the office can be held to account.
options: A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.
Both A and R are true, but R does not explain A.
Both A and R are true, and R explains A.
questions.explanation: The charter makes the standard public, which is the basis of accountability.

questions.label: Expected – Practice
questions.stem: The "Koshi Declaration, 2083" was issued by which gathering?
options: A meeting of the seven Province Chiefs
The Inter-Province Chief Ministers' Conference at Biratnagar
questions.explanation: It was issued in Ashoj 2083 and dealt with fiscal federalism, the Federal Civil Service Bill and provincial police. 🔄

topics.title: Main economic indicators (मुख्य आर्थिक सूचक)

questions.label: Expected – Practice
questions.stem: According to the Economic Survey 2082/83, what economic growth rate was estimated for fiscal year 2082/83?
questions.explanation: 3.85 percent is the preliminary estimate. 4.43 percent is the revised figure for 2081/82; 6 percent was the aim of the budget for 2082/83 and 7 percent is the aim for 2083/84. 🔄

questions.label: Pattern-Based – Reconstructed
questions.stem:
Match the term with its meaning.

  1. Gross Domestic Product — A. GDP plus net income received from abroad
  2. Gross National Income — B. A general and continuing rise in prices
  3. Inflation — C. Value of the final goods and services produced inside the country in a year
  4. Per capita income — D. National income divided by the population
questions.explanation: GDP is production inside the country; GNI adds net income from abroad; inflation is a rise in prices; per capita means per person.

questions.label: Pattern-Based – Reconstructed
questions.stem:
Consider these statements about the make-up of Nepal's GDP in 2082/83.

  1. Services give the largest share of GDP.
  2. Agriculture, forestry and fishing give about 24 percent.
  3. Industry gives more than half of GDP.

Which of them are correct?
questions.explanation: Services give about 62 percent and agriculture about 24 percent. Industry gives only about 14 percent. 🔄

questions.label: Expected – Practice
questions.stem: Which body prepares Nepal's national accounts, including the estimate of GDP?
questions.explanation: The National Statistics Office, formerly the Central Bureau of Statistics. The Ministry of Finance uses its figures in the Economic Survey.

questions.label: Expected – Practice
questions.stem: By the estimates for 2082/83, which province has the lowest GDP per person?
questions.explanation: Madhesh, USD 934. Karnali has the smallest economy in total, but its GDP per person (USD 1,108) is higher than that of Madhesh. 🔄

topics.title: Agriculture and land (कृषि र भूमि)

questions.label: Expected – Practice
questions.stem: Under the Land Act, 2021 as it now stands, what is the basic ceiling on land-holding in the Terai and Inner Madhesh?
questions.explanation: 10 bigha. The ceilings are 25 ropani in the Kathmandu Valley and 70 ropani in other hill areas. The original Act of 2021 had allowed 25 bigha.

questions.label: Pattern-Based – Reconstructed
questions.stem:
Match the crop with a district commonly named for it.

  1. Tea — A. Jumla
  2. Coffee — B. Ilam
  3. Apple — C. Gulmi
  4. Jute — D. Morang
questions.explanation: Tea–Ilam, coffee–Gulmi, apple–Jumla, jute–Morang.

questions.label: Pattern-Based – Reconstructed
questions.stem: Fill in the blank. In the land measures of the Terai, one bigha equals ______ kattha.
questions.explanation: One bigha is 20 kattha and one kattha is 20 dhur. Sixteen is the number of aana in one ropani.

questions.label: Expected – Practice
questions.stem: According to the National Agricultural Census, 2078, what is the average land operated by a farm family?
questions.explanation: 0.55 hectare. It was 0.68 hectare in the census of 2068, so holdings are getting smaller.

questions.label: Pattern-Based – Reconstructed
questions.stem:
Consider these statements.

  1. In the census of 2078, 57.3 percent of employed people worked in agriculture, forestry and fishing.
  2. Agriculture, forestry and fishing gave about 24 percent of GDP in 2082/83.
  3. The Agriculture Development Strategy covers the years 2015 to 2035.

Which of them are correct?
questions.explanation: All three are correct. Together, statements 1 and 2 show how low the output per farm worker is.

topics.title: Industry, trade and investment (उद्योग, व्यापार र लगानी)

questions.label: Expected – Practice
questions.stem: Under the Industrial Enterprises Act, 2076, an industry is "large" when its fixed capital is more than:
questions.explanation: Above Rs 50 crore is large. Rs 15 crore is the upper limit of a small industry.

questions.label: Pattern-Based – Reconstructed
questions.stem:
Consider these statements about Nepal's foreign trade in 2082/83.

  1. Imports were more than Rs 2,000 billion.
  2. Exports were larger than imports.
  3. Soybean oil was the largest export item.

Which of them are correct?
questions.explanation: Imports were Rs 2,096.38 billion and exports only Rs 315.29 billion, so statement 2 is wrong. Soybean oil made up 40.8 percent of exports. 🔄

questions.label: Expected – Practice
questions.stem: Which is the oldest industrial estate (औद्योगिक क्षेत्र) of Nepal?
questions.explanation: Balaju, set up in 2016 BS (1960). Hetauda and Patan followed in 2020 BS.

questions.label: Pattern-Based – Reconstructed
questions.stem:
Match the body or law with what it does.

  1. Investment Board Nepal — A. Approves foreign investment in smaller projects
  2. Department of Industry — B. Records exports and imports at the border
  3. Department of Customs — C. Handles investment projects of more than Rs 6 billion
  4. Special Economic Zone Act, 2073 — D. Gives export industries a zone with special facilities
questions.explanation: The Board takes the large projects, the Department of Industry the smaller ones, Customs keeps the trade figures, and the Act of 2073 creates the zones.

questions.label: Pattern-Based – Reconstructed
questions.stem: Three of these are counted in the balance of trade in goods. Which one is not?
options: Remittance sent home by workers abroad
questions.explanation: Remittance is a transfer of money, not trade in goods. It enters the balance of payments.

topics.title: Tourism (पर्यटन)

questions.label: Expected – Practice
questions.stem: Which country sent the largest number of tourists to Nepal in 2025?
questions.explanation: India sent 292,438 of the 1,158,459 tourists, about a quarter. The United States was second and China third. 🔄

questions.label: Pattern-Based – Reconstructed
questions.stem: Fill in the blank. The Government has declared the years ______ as the Nepal Tourism Decade.
questions.explanation: 2023 to 2032, with a target of 3.5 million tourists a year by 2032.

questions.label: Pattern-Based – Reconstructed
questions.stem:
Arrange these in order of time, the earliest first.

  1. Nepal Tourism Year, with a target of one million tourists
  2. The first Visit Nepal Year
  3. The start of the Nepal Tourism Decade
  4. Visit Nepal 2020, which was postponed
questions.explanation: Visit Nepal Year 1998, Nepal Tourism Year 2011, Visit Nepal 2020, and the Decade from 2023.

questions.label: Expected – Practice
questions.stem: Which body, set up in 1998 as a partnership of the Government and the private tourism industry, promotes Nepal as a destination?
questions.explanation: The Nepal Tourism Board. The Department of Tourism issues expedition permits.

questions.label: Pattern-Based – Reconstructed
questions.stem:
Consider these statements.

  1. Nepal received 1,158,459 foreign tourists in 2025.
  2. India was the largest source of tourists in 2025.
  3. The Tourism Decade aims at ten million tourists a year by 2032.

Which of them are correct?
questions.explanation: The target of the Decade is 3.5 million a year, not ten million. 🔄

topics.title: Development infrastructure (विकास पूर्वाधार)

questions.label: Expected – Practice
questions.stem: How many international airports are in operation in Nepal?
questions.explanation: Tribhuvan (Kathmandu), Gautam Buddha (Bhairahawa) and Pokhara. Nijgadh is a proposed airport. 🔄

questions.label: Pattern-Based – Reconstructed
questions.stem:
Match the airport with its place.

  1. Gautam Buddha International Airport — A. Lukla, Solukhumbu
  2. Tenzing–Hillary Airport — B. Bhairahawa, Rupandehi
  3. Tribhuvan International Airport — C. Kathmandu
  4. Talcha Airport — D. Near Rara Lake, Mugu
questions.explanation: Gautam Buddha–Bhairahawa, Tenzing–Hillary–Lukla, Tribhuvan–Kathmandu, Talcha–Mugu.

questions.label: Expected – Practice
questions.stem: The Nagdhunga–Sisnekhola tunnel, described as Nepal's first modern road tunnel, was opened in:
questions.explanation: It was opened on 11 Shrawan 2083 (27 July 2026). The main tunnel is 2.688 km long. 🔄

questions.label: Pattern-Based – Reconstructed
questions.stem:
Consider these statements, based on the Economic Survey 2082/83.

  1. The Mid-Hill (Pushpalal) Highway runs through the Terai.
  2. The roads of the three levels together are more than 100,000 km long.
  3. More than half of the federal road network is blacktopped.

Which of them are correct?
questions.explanation: The Mid-Hill Highway runs through the hills; the road through the Terai is the Postal Highway. All roads together are 104,906 km, and 55.6 percent of the federal network is blacktopped. 🔄

questions.label: Pattern-Based – Reconstructed
questions.stem:
Arrange these in order of time, the earliest first.

  1. Royal Nepal Airlines Corporation is founded
  2. The Raxaul–Amlekhganj railway opens
  3. Pokhara International Airport opens
  4. The Manakamana Cable Car opens
questions.explanation: Railway 1927, airline 1958, cable car 1998, airport 2023.

topics.title: Planned development and the periodic plans (योजनाबद्ध विकास र आवधिक योजना)

questions.label: Expected – Practice
questions.stem: Which period does the Sixteenth Plan cover?
questions.explanation: Fiscal years 2081/82 to 2085/86. The period 2076/77–2080/81 belonged to the Fifteenth Plan.

questions.label: Pattern-Based – Reconstructed
questions.stem:
Match the plan with its feature.

  1. First Plan — A. Poverty alleviation as the single main objective
  2. Ninth Plan — B. Began in 2013 BS
  3. Tenth Plan — C. Carried the long-term vision "Prosperous Nepal, Happy Nepali"
  4. Fifteenth Plan — D. Also served as the Poverty Reduction Strategy Paper
questions.explanation: First Plan–2013 BS; Ninth–poverty alleviation; Tenth–Poverty Reduction Strategy Paper; Fifteenth–vision 2100.

questions.label: Expected – Practice
questions.stem: Who chairs the National Planning Commission?
questions.explanation: The Prime Minister is the Chairperson. The Vice-Chairperson leads the daily work.

questions.label: Pattern-Based – Reconstructed
questions.stem:
Consider these statements about the Sixteenth Plan.

  1. It is a three-year plan.
  2. Its vision is "good governance, social justice and prosperity".
  3. It aims to bring absolute poverty down to 12 percent.

Which of them are correct?
questions.explanation: The Sixteenth Plan is a five-year plan (2081/82–2085/86). The other two statements are correct.

questions.label: Expected – Practice
questions.stem: Of the fifteen periodic plans completed before the Sixteenth Plan, how many were three-year plans?
questions.explanation: Five: the Second, Eleventh, Twelfth, Thirteenth and Fourteenth. The other ten were five-year plans.

topics.title: Budget system and the current budget (बजेट प्रणाली र चालू बजेट)

questions.label: Expected – Practice
questions.stem: Under Article 122, the advance spending allowed by a vote on account may not be more than what share of the year's estimated expenditure?
questions.explanation: One third. A vote on account lets the Government spend while the Appropriation Bill is still being discussed.

questions.label: Pattern-Based – Reconstructed
questions.stem:
Match the Article with its subject.

  1. Article 116 — A. Federal Contingency Fund
  2. Article 119 — B. Federal Consolidated Fund
  3. Article 122 — C. Estimates of revenue and expenditure
  4. Article 124 — D. Votes on account
questions.explanation: 116 Consolidated Fund; 119 estimates (the budget); 122 votes on account; 124 Contingency Fund.

questions.label: Expected – Practice
questions.stem: Who presented Nepal's first budget, on 21 Magh 2008 BS?
questions.explanation: Subarna Shamsher, as Finance Minister. The budget was of about Rs 5.25 crore.

questions.label: Pattern-Based – Reconstructed
questions.stem:
Consider these statements about the federal budget for 2083/84.

  1. Its total is Rs 2,124.34 billion.
  2. It aims at economic growth of 7 percent.
  3. More money is set aside for capital expenditure than for current expenditure.

Which of them are correct?
questions.explanation: Current expenditure takes 59.8 percent and capital expenditure only 20.3 percent, so statement 3 is wrong. 🔄

questions.label: Pattern-Based – Reconstructed
questions.stem:
Arrange the stages of the budget cycle in the right order.

  1. Ministries prepare their programmes within the ceilings
  2. The Auditor General audits the accounts
  3. Parliament passes the Appropriation Bill
  4. Offices spend the money during the fiscal year
questions.explanation: Formulation, approval, implementation, then audit.

topics.title: Revenue, taxation and public debt (राजस्व, कर र सार्वजनिक ऋण)

questions.label: Expected – Practice
questions.stem: What is the standard rate of value-added tax in Nepal?
questions.explanation: 13 percent. The tax began at 10 percent in 2054 BS, and the budget for 2083/84 left the rate unchanged.

questions.label: Pattern-Based – Reconstructed
questions.stem: Three of these are indirect taxes. Which one is a direct tax?
questions.explanation: Income tax is borne by the person who earns the income. The other three are passed on to the buyer in the price.

questions.label: Pattern-Based – Reconstructed
questions.stem:
Match the office with its work.

  1. Inland Revenue Department — A. Keeps the accounts of government revenue and spending
  2. Department of Customs — B. Administers income tax, value-added tax and excise
  3. Financial Comptroller General Office — C. Manages government borrowing and its records
  4. Public Debt Management Office — D. Collects duty on goods crossing the border
questions.explanation: Inland Revenue–internal taxes; Customs–border duty; Comptroller General–accounts; Debt Management Office–borrowing.

questions.label: Expected – Practice
questions.stem: From which date was value-added tax applied in Nepal?
questions.explanation: 1 Mangsir 2054 (16 November 1997), under the Act of 2052. The day is kept as National Tax Day.

questions.label: Pattern-Based – Reconstructed
questions.stem:
Consider these statements about Nepal's public debt.

  1. It had passed Rs 3,000 billion by mid-October 2026.
  2. External debt is a larger part of it than internal debt.
  3. It is equal to about 45 percent of GDP.

Which of them are correct?
questions.explanation: All three are correct: Rs 3,009.11 billion in mid-October 2026; about 54 percent of it external; about 45 percent of GDP. 🔄

topics.title: Banking, money and Nepal Rastra Bank (बैंकिङ, मुद्रा र नेपाल राष्ट्र बैंक)

questions.label: Expected – Practice
questions.stem: Under the Banks and Financial Institutions Act, 2073, to which class do development banks belong?
questions.explanation: Class B. Commercial banks are Class A, finance companies Class C and microfinance institutions Class D.

questions.label: Pattern-Based – Reconstructed
questions.stem:
Match the tool with its rate in the monetary policy for 2083/84.

  1. Bank rate — A. 4 percent
  2. Policy rate — B. 2.75 percent
  3. Deposit collection rate — C. 5.75 percent
  4. Cash reserve ratio — D. 4.25 percent
questions.explanation: Bank rate 5.75, policy rate 4.25, deposit collection rate 2.75 and cash reserve ratio 4 percent. 🔄

questions.label: Expected – Practice
questions.stem: At what fixed rate is the Nepali rupee tied to the Indian rupee?
questions.explanation: Rs 1.60, unchanged since 2049 BS (February 1993).

questions.label: Pattern-Based – Reconstructed
questions.stem:
Arrange these by date of founding, the earliest first.

  1. Rastriya Banijya Bank
  2. Nepal Rastra Bank
  3. Nepal Bank Limited
  4. Agricultural Development Bank
questions.explanation: Nepal Bank 1994 BS, Nepal Rastra Bank 2013, Rastriya Banijya Bank 2022, Agricultural Development Bank 2024.

questions.label: Pattern-Based – Reconstructed
questions.stem:
Consider these statements.

  1. Nepal Rastra Bank issues the monetary policy.
  2. The Securities Board of Nepal regulates insurance companies.
  3. The monetary policy for 2083/84 is the 25th yearly monetary policy.

Which of them are correct?
questions.explanation: Insurance is regulated by the Nepal Insurance Authority; the Securities Board regulates the share market.

topics.title: Poverty, employment, remittance, graduation and the Sustainable Development Goals (गरिबी, रोजगारी, विप्रेषण, स्तरोन्नति र दिगो विकास लक्ष्य)

questions.label: Expected – Practice
questions.stem: According to the fourth Nepal Living Standards Survey (2079/80), what share of the people live below the poverty line?
questions.explanation: 20.27 percent. The figures 30.85 and 25.16 come from the second and third surveys; 17.4 percent is multidimensional poverty.

questions.label: Pattern-Based – Reconstructed
questions.stem: Fill in the blank. The Sustainable Development Goals have 17 goals and ______ targets.
questions.explanation: 169 targets, to be reached by 2030.

questions.label: Expected – Practice
questions.stem: By its resolution of 29 October 2026, the United Nations General Assembly moved the date of Nepal's graduation from the least-developed-country category to:
questions.explanation: 24 November 2029, three years after the earlier date of 24 November 2026. The same resolution covers Bangladesh. 🔄

questions.label: Pattern-Based – Reconstructed
questions.stem:
Match the number of the Sustainable Development Goal with its subject.

  1. Goal 1 — A. Quality education
  2. Goal 4 — B. Climate action
  3. Goal 5 — C. No poverty
  4. Goal 13 — D. Gender equality
questions.explanation: Goal 1 no poverty; Goal 4 quality education; Goal 5 gender equality; Goal 13 climate action.

questions.label: Pattern-Based – Reconstructed
questions.stem:
Consider these statements about the list of least developed countries.

  1. Nepal left the list on 24 November 2026.
  2. Nepal has been on the list since 1971.
  3. Three criteria are used to decide whether a country may graduate.

Which of them are correct?
questions.explanation: Nepal has not left the list; in October 2026 its graduation was moved to 24 November 2029. 🔄

topics.title: End-of-chapter test — Top 25

questions.label: Expected – Practice
questions.stem: Which Part of the Constitution contains the federal financial procedures, Articles 115 to 125?
questions.explanation: Part 10. Part 11 is on the judiciary.

questions.label: Expected – Practice
questions.stem: Gross National Income is equal to Gross Domestic Product plus:
questions.explanation: GNI adds to GDP the income received from abroad minus the income paid abroad.

questions.label: Pattern-Based – Reconstructed
questions.stem:
Match the document or figure with the body that issues it.

  1. Economic Survey — A. Nepal Rastra Bank
  2. Monetary policy — B. National Planning Commission
  3. Periodic plan — C. Ministry of Finance
  4. Foreign-trade figures — D. Department of Customs
questions.explanation: Economic Survey–Ministry of Finance; monetary policy–Nepal Rastra Bank; periodic plan–National Planning Commission; trade figures–Department of Customs.

questions.label: Expected – Practice
questions.stem: By the estimates for 2082/83, which province produces the largest share of Nepal's GDP?
questions.explanation: Bagmati, 36.7 percent. Koshi is second with 15.8 percent. 🔄

questions.label: Pattern-Based – Reconstructed
questions.stem: Fill in the blank. A GDP of 66 kharba 9 arba rupees is the same as Rs ______ billion.
questions.explanation: One kharba is 100 arba, and one arba is one billion: 66 × 100 + 9 = 6,609.

questions.label: Expected – Practice
questions.stem: The National Agricultural Census of 2078 BS was Nepal's:
questions.explanation: The seventh. An agricultural census is taken every ten years.

questions.label: Pattern-Based – Reconstructed
questions.stem:
Consider these statements about land.

  1. One ropani has 16 aana.
  2. One bigha is smaller than one ropani.
  3. The Land Act, 2021 sets a ceiling of 25 ropani in the Kathmandu Valley.

Which of them are correct?
questions.explanation: One bigha is about 13.31 ropani, so statement 2 is wrong.

questions.label: Expected – Practice
questions.stem: On which date did the Government declare the kamaiya (bonded labour) system ended?
questions.explanation: 2 Shrawan 2057 (17 July 2000). The date 21 Bhadra 2065 belongs to the haliya.

questions.label: Pattern-Based – Reconstructed
questions.stem: A factory has fixed capital of Rs 30 crore. Under the Industrial Enterprises Act, 2076, it is a:
questions.explanation: A medium industry has fixed capital of more than Rs 15 crore and up to Rs 50 crore.

questions.label: Expected – Practice
questions.stem: With which country does Nepal carry on the largest share of its foreign trade?
questions.explanation: India. In 2082/83 Nepal imported about Rs 1,210 billion from India and exported about Rs 258 billion to it — about 61 percent of all trade. 🔄

questions.label: Expected – Practice
questions.stem: In which year did Nepal become the 147th member of the World Trade Organization?
questions.explanation: 23 April 2004 (11 Baisakh 2061).

questions.label: Pattern-Based – Reconstructed
questions.stem:
Match the tourism campaign with its target.

  1. Visit Nepal Year 1998 — A. 2 million tourists
  2. Nepal Tourism Year 2011 — B. 3.5 million tourists a year
  3. Visit Nepal 2020 — C. 500,000 tourists
  4. Tourism Decade, by 2032 — D. 1 million tourists
questions.explanation: 1998: half a million; 2011: one million; 2020: two million; the Decade: 3.5 million a year.

questions.label: Pattern-Based – Reconstructed
questions.stem: Three of these are international airports in operation. Which one is not?
questions.explanation: Nijgadh is a proposed airport. 🔄

questions.label: Expected – Practice
questions.stem: How long is the Mid-Hill (Pushpalal) Highway planned to be?
questions.explanation: 1,879 km. The Mahendra Highway is about 1,028 km and the Postal Highway 1,857 km.

questions.label: Pattern-Based – Reconstructed
questions.stem:
Arrange these plans in order of time, the earliest first.

  1. Eleventh Plan (the Three-Year Interim Plan)
  2. Fifteenth Plan
